work_completed: `src/gov/accept/runner.py`: `_remove` now runs up to 20 removal passes (`_remove_pass`), with short growing waits between them, until the folder is gone. It never raises: an error that is still there after the last pass is passed over. Within a pass, an entry already gone or changed meanwhile is skipped, and a folder refilled after it was emptied is cleaned again by the next pass. Each folder is listed once, and the names still to do are kept per level, so a pass is linear in the entries. Before that, every descent re-listed its parent, which is why the time grew with the square. There is still no recursion, no long path, one open descriptor at a time, and links are removed, never followed. New safeguard: each move up through `..` is checked against the parent's device and inode, so a folder another process moves away cannot lead the removal outside the private folder. The old code would have deleted files outside in that case; a test shows it. `_run`'s signal holding (R9), the 128+N exit (R12) and the kept ignore (R11) are unchanged; since `_remove` no longer raises, a stopped run keeps 128+N and an unstopped run is never turned into `crash` by the clean-up.

discoveries: (1) The old removal could also leave the private tree: if a folder was moved elsewhere while it was being emptied, going up through `..` landed in the new parent and deleted its contents. The device and inode check closes this, and `test_w2_96_r14_the_removal_never_leaves_the_tree` covers it. (2) Inside the sandbox, 11 placeholder files (character device 1,3) appear as untracked at the worktree root: `.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.mcp.json`, `.idea`, `.vscode` and others. They are not real files, so I neither staged nor touched them. (3) No linter (ruff, pyflakes) is installed here.
risks: A clean-up that meets an error that never goes away now waits about 4 s over its 20 passes before passing it over, with the signals held. A process that keeps writing after the last pass, or that recreates folders with `makedirs`, can still leave entries behind; no removal can prevent that without being able to stop the process. `pytest-of-usain/pytest-0` (retained folders of my red run's failed tests, inside my TMPDIR) is still there because the guard refused its removal.
lessons: Racing removals can be reproduced in unit tests by wrapping `os.unlink`/`os.rmdir` (the wrapper removes the entry, then calls again) and by a writer started in its own session from inside a planted test. The wrapper should only act on `dir_fd` calls so it hits only the clean-up. A writer in such a test must use `os.mkdir`, not `makedirs`, or it recreates the caller's TMPDIR tree after the clean-up.
